title: How to Build an Emergency Fund on a Low Income (Step by Step)

scenes.heading: Your car just broke
lines: Imagine this. Your car breaks down, and the mechanic says: four hundred dollars.

scenes.heading: Could you pay it?
lines: Could you pay that right now, in cash? Be honest.

scenes.heading: You're not alone
lines: If the answer is no, you are not alone. Not even close.

scenes.heading: 1 in 3
lines: More than a third of American adults couldn't cover a four hundred dollar surprise with cash.

scenes.heading: Here's the fix
lines: So today, I'll show you how to build an emergency fund, even on a small paycheck.

scenes.heading: The debt trap
lines: Here's what happens without one. Every surprise goes straight onto a credit card.
scenes.chapter: Why You Need a Safety Net

scenes.heading: It snowballs
lines: Then the interest makes next month even tighter. And the cycle repeats.

scenes.heading: Not your fault
lines: It's not because you're bad with money. Life is just unpredictable.

scenes.heading: Break the cycle
lines: An emergency fund is the wall between you and new debt.

scenes.heading: Forget 6 months
lines: You've heard you need six months of expenses saved. On a low income, that feels impossible.

scenes.heading: Start small
lines: So forget that for now. Your first goal is just five hundred dollars.

scenes.heading: $500 = peace
lines: That alone covers a car repair, a new phone screen, or a surprise bill.

scenes.heading: Then level up
lines: Hit it? Great. Now aim for one thousand.

scenes.heading: Money leaks
lines: Step two. Find the money that's already slipping away.

scenes.heading: Forgotten apps
lines: Subscriptions you forgot about. Apps you never open.

scenes.heading: Bank fees?!
lines: Overdraft fees. Monthly account fees. Many banks offer accounts without them.

scenes.heading: Daily extras
lines: And those little daily extras. Snacks, delivery fees, impulse buys.

scenes.heading: $720 a year
lines: Just sixty dollars a month is seven hundred and twenty dollars a year!

scenes.heading: Every week
lines: Step three. Pick an amount you can save every single week, no matter how small.

scenes.heading: $10 a week
lines: Ten dollars a week becomes five hundred and twenty dollars in a year.

scenes.heading: $25 a week
lines: Twenty five a week? That's thirteen hundred.

scenes.heading: $50 a week
lines: Fifty a week? Twenty six hundred dollars!

scenes.heading: Habit wins
lines: The amount matters less than the habit. Consistency builds the fund.

scenes.heading: Automate it
lines: Step four. Take willpower out of the game completely.

scenes.heading: Payday transfer
lines: Set up an automatic transfer to savings on payday.

scenes.heading: Split it
lines: Many banks let you split your direct deposit, so part of every paycheck lands in savings by itself.

scenes.heading: Out of sight
lines: Money you never see in checking is money you won't spend.

scenes.heading: Keep it apart
lines: Step five. Where you keep this money matters.

scenes.heading: Not in checking
lines: If it sits in your checking account, it will disappear. Trust me.

scenes.heading: Separate savings
lines: Put it in a separate savings account, ideally high yield, at a federally insured bank or credit union.

scenes.heading: Don't invest it
lines: And don't invest it. It needs to be there, at full value, the moment you need it.

scenes.heading: Turbo boost
lines: Want to get there faster? Use money that isn't part of your paycheck.
scenes.chapter: Step 6: Boost It With Extra Cash

scenes.heading: Tax refund
lines: A tax refund can fill your starter fund in a single day.

scenes.heading: Side cash
lines: A few hours of side work. Selling stuff you don't use anymore.

scenes.heading: Half of it
lines: Rule of thumb: send at least half of any surprise money straight to the fund.

scenes.heading: Real emergencies
lines: Step seven. Decide ahead of time what counts as an emergency.

scenes.heading: Yes
lines: A car repair you need for work, a medical bill, losing your job? Yes.

scenes.heading: No!
lines: A big sale, a concert, a holiday trip? No. Those get their own savings goal.

scenes.heading: Refill it
lines: And if you use it? That's okay. That's what it's for. Just start refilling it.

scenes.heading: The roadmap
lines: Here's the full roadmap. First, five hundred. Then one thousand.

scenes.heading: 3 months
lines: Then three months of essentials: rent, food, utilities, transport.

scenes.heading: 6 months
lines: And over time, six months. Every stage makes you safer than before.

scenes.heading: You can do this
lines: You don't need a big income to build a safety net. You just need to start.

scenes.heading: Your turn
lines: If this helped, subscribe for one simple money move every day.

scenes.heading: Tell me
lines: And tell me in the comments: what's your first savings goal?
